correctness.rationale: The exact private-pair iff criterion is proved by a single-negative trace and graph components of the selected negative witness edges. Unique-coordinate changes forbid cycles in the full witness graph; equality forces a tree and determines each split as an edge cut, uniquely reconstructed by separation distances. The all-positive branch of any complete mistake tree must successively refine the common split atoms, yielding Ldim at most n-1. Direct Bell-partition trace checks for all 32,768 possible n=5 split supports and every smaller n agree with the criterion and all Prüfer tree cut certificates; n<=4 exact Littlestone recurrence agrees. The n=4,5 facet census is explicitly computational and does not assert an all-n profile.

evidence: Koppelberg (1989), Handbook of Boolean Algebras vol.1 Section 4.4 Definition 4.21 defines no element in the subalgebra generated by others as irredundance; Proposition 4.23 says maximally irredundant families generate dense subalgebras.
For a finite powerset algebra, a shore is generated by others exactly when it is constant on each atom of their common refinement. Its negation gives the private crossing-pair criterion.

originality.rationale: Classical Boolean-algebra irredundance is an EXACT equivalent formulation and is openly acknowledged; the 1989 Handbook definition and its maximal-irredundant density proposition are not new and not claimed to be. The inspected primary partition-learning papers query pairwise same-cluster relations, not saturation of arbitrary splits. The 2023 injective split systems paper studies median/Buneman structures, not traces of all hidden partitions. The specific learning interpretation plus exact online n-1, labeled-tree bijection and n^(n-2) highest-face count and nonpure facet data were not found in compared primary literature or the published indexed-search matches. The potential existence of an earlier enumeration of irredundant generators of finite powerset Boolean algebras is expressly retained as the main priority risk.
residual_risks: The classical Boolean-algebra irredundant-family language exactly matches the private-pair characterization; an unlocated specialist account could have proved the Cayley tree correspondence and face enumerations already.
Not all historical literature on finite Boolean generating sets, split-system test families, or online learning has been exhaustively inspected.
The small-polynomial and facet computations are exhaustive only for n<=5; no all-n middle-face formula or external independent audit is claimed.

value.rationale: The natural predicate asks whether an arbitrary proposed bipartition respects every cluster in the unknown partition. A complete private-crossing-pair test recognizes every shattered support. Every extremal support is canonically a vertex-labeled tree edge-cut system, giving an exact n^(n-2) maximal-size family count. VC and online dimensions equal n-1 despite Bell(n) concepts, and the finite facet census reveals nonpurity already at n=4. This is motivated structure beyond a cheap scalar invariant or arbitrary finite numerical example.
